name: PixiTween Director S9: Local mode on Muse Glimmer
description: Local mode: chat edits (and frame review when the reviewer hook is adopted) run on Muse Glimmer 30B through Ollama's native API for privacy, offline use and zero cost, with automatic fallback when the Meta API fails, a typed Spark Open stub, a toggle and badge, and an owner-run A/B script. The route lives in handlers/local.ts, the UI in the BackendBadge stub S9 owns. Never positioned as faster than Spark.

readFirst: docs/hackathon/06-contracts.md (LlmBackend, ToolDef, FilmEvent, authoring core API)
docs/hackathon/steps/step-09-open-weight-lane/design.md (sections 3, 5, 6, 7 and 11: routing, Glimmer rules, verified Ollama facts)
docs/hackathon/steps/step-09-open-weight-lane/contract-issues.md (which gaps the contract update resolved; what remains)
docs/hackathon/06-contracts.md sections 5 (GET/PUT /api/local-mode) and 6 (D-1, D-5, D-6, D-8, D-10)
fixtures/seed/README.md and fixtures/seed/glimmer-*.json (the seed transcripts are summaries)
server/llm/backend.ts, server/llm/router.ts, server/llm/spark-backend.ts and server/meta/http.ts (S2) before writing any adapter
extraGuardrails: Never contact Ollama, Baseten or the Meta API from a story or a test: use the node:http mock server and the fixtures. The s09-local script is created, never run.
Always send think:false and use the format field (never response_format) on Ollama's native /api/chat; encode these rules in tests.
Never claim Muse Glimmer is faster than Muse Spark, and never write 'fully offline' for the product (design sections 1 and 10).
Do not edit server/http/routes.ts, server/http/middleware.ts or web/src/panels/Chat.tsx: routes register through handlers/local.ts (06 D-1), and S6's Chat already renders <BackendBadge /> (D-6).

Read GLIMMER_BASE_URL, GLIMMER_MODEL, LOCAL_MODE, EDIT_BACKEND, BASETEN_API_KEY and GLIMMER_NUM_CTX from the validated env object (06 D-8); never read process.env for them and never edit server/env.ts.
manualGates: MG-1 (owner, Ollama running with muse-glimmer:30b-mlx pulled, $0): npm run live -- s09-local --yes. Paste the printed table into steps/step-09-open-weight-lane/ab.md. At least 5 of 6 edits correct; any 'context truncation suspected' warning explained.
MG-1b (optional, about $0.01 of API calls, owner approves): npm run live -- s09-local --with-spark --yes for the Spark side of the A/B.

MG-2 (optional, owner approves a 65 GB download): GLIMMER_MODEL=muse-glimmer:30b-mlx-bf16-dflash npm run live -- s09-local --yes; keep that build only if it is at least 1.5 times faster on the same edits.

MG-3 (owner): record the Wi-Fi-off clip with the checklist in design section 9 (terminal showing ollama ps, toggle on, three edits with the badge, the new-art boundary hint, one Spark edit for contrast).
MG-4 (owner): confirm on the hosted demo that the toggle is disabled with the reason 'Ollama is not reachable'.

stories.title: Transcript fixtures: rebuild raw Ollama responses from seed summaries
stories.description: As a test author, I want the seed Glimmer transcripts turned into raw Ollama responses so that backend tests replay real shapes without a model.
steps: Read fixtures/seed/README.md, fixtures/seed/glimmer-scene-turns.json and fixtures/seed/glimmer-edit-1-turns.json (they are per-turn summaries: ms, status, calls as 'name(argsJSON)' strings, content), and docs/hackathon/steps/step-09-open-weight-lane/design.md sections 4.1 and 4.2.

Create fixtures/s09/transcripts.ts exporting parseCallSummary(s: string): { name: string; args: Record<string, unknown> } (name = text before the first '(', args = JSON.parse of the text between the first '(' and the last ')'), type TranscriptTurn = { ms: number; status: number; calls: string[]; content: string }, loadTranscript(name: 'scene' | 'edit-1'): TranscriptTurn[] (reads the seed JSON with node:fs relative to the repository root), and toOllamaResponse(turn: TranscriptTurn, model = 'muse-glimmer:30b-mlx').

toOllamaResponse returns the documented shape { model, created_at: '2026-10-27T00:00:00Z', message: { role: 'assistant', content, tool_calls?: [{ function: { name, arguments } }] }, done: true, done_reason: 'stop', total_duration: turn.ms * 1e6, load_duration: 10000000, prompt_eval_count: 71, prompt_eval_duration: 590000000, eval_count: 104, eval_duration: 4900000000 }. Omit tool_calls when there are no calls. Comment the constants: they are shape-only sample values taken from the S1 throughput sample, not measurements for any run.
Create fixtures/s09/transcripts.test.ts.
acceptance: loadTranscript('scene') has 4 turns with call counts [1, 3, 2, 0] and ms values [17004, 20788, 24309, 4065]; loadTranscript('edit-1') has 2 turns with call counts [2, 0]
parseCallSummary('setKeyframes({"layerId":"mug","property":"scale","keys":[[0,1],[6,1.25]],"ease":"easeInOut"})') returns name 'setKeyframes' and args.keys equal to [[0,1],[6,1.25]]
toOllamaResponse of the last scene turn has message.content 'DONE', no tool_calls key, done true and total_duration 4065000000
toOllamaResponse of the first edit-1 turn has message.tool_calls with 2 entries whose function.arguments are objects, not strings

stories.title: Parse Ollama chat responses into tool calls and usage
stories.description: As a backend developer, I want a pure parser for Ollama's native chat response so that tool calls, ids and timing are extracted in one tested place.
steps: Read docs/hackathon/steps/step-09-open-weight-lane/design.md sections 4.1 and 4.3 (arguments is a JSON object, there is no tool-call id, durations are nanoseconds), server/llm/backend.ts (S2) for the ToolCall shape, and fixtures/s09/transcripts.ts.

Create server/llm/glimmer/errors.ts exporting class GlimmerError extends Error with a code of 'unreachable' | 'http' | 'tool-parse' | 'invalid-json' | 'timeout' | 'model-missing', an optional numeric status, and name 'GlimmerError'.

Create server/llm/glimmer/parse.ts exporting parseOllamaChat(raw: unknown, opts?: { turn?: number; wallMs?: number }): { toolCalls: Array<{ id: string; name: string; args: Record<string, unknown> }>; content: string; ms: number; usage: { promptTokens?: number; outputTokens?: number; tokPerSec?: number }; doneReason?: string }.

Rules: ids are 'glimmer-<turn>-<index>' (turn defaults to 0); arguments that are strings are JSON.parse'd and a parse failure throws GlimmerError('tool-parse'); a response without a message object throws GlimmerError('http', undefined, 'response has no message'); ms = Math.round(total_duration / 1e6) when numeric, else opts.wallMs ?? 0; tokPerSec = eval_count / (eval_duration / 1e9) rounded to one decimal when both are positive numbers; content is the message content string ('' when absent); the 'thinking' field is ignored.
Create server/llm/glimmer/parse.test.ts using toOllamaResponse from fixtures/s09/transcripts.ts.
acceptance: For scene turn index 1 (3 calls) with opts.turn 1 the ids are 'glimmer-1-0', 'glimmer-1-1' and 'glimmer-1-2', content is '' and ms is 20788
With the sample stats (eval_count 104, eval_duration 4.9e9) usage.tokPerSec is 21.2 and usage.promptTokens is 71
A call whose arguments is the string '{"a":1}' yields args { a: 1 }, and the string '{bad' throws a GlimmerError whose code is 'tool-parse'
parseOllamaChat({}) throws a GlimmerError with code 'http'; with no total_duration and opts.wallMs 1234, ms is 1234

stories.title: Convert tool definitions to Ollama tools with Glimmer hints
stories.description: As a backend developer, I want tool schemas converted with explicit z and keys descriptions so that the model uses depth and keyframes the way S1 showed it needs.
steps: Read docs/hackathon/steps/step-09-open-weight-lane/design.md sections 5.1 and 6, shared/tools.ts (ToolDef) and server/llm/spark-backend.ts (S2) to see how it turns ToolDef.params (zod) into JSON schema; reuse an exported helper if one exists, otherwise use zodToJsonSchema from 'zod-to-json-schema' directly with $refStrategy 'none'.

Create server/llm/glimmer/schema.ts exporting type OllamaTool = { type: 'function'; function: { name: string; description: string; parameters: Record<string, unknown> } } and toOllamaTools(tools: ToolDef[]): OllamaTool[] preserving order, deleting any '$schema' key, and applying augmentToolSchemas.

Export Z_HINT = 'Depth. Larger = further from the camera; the background has the largest z.' and KEYS_HINT = 'Keyframes as [timeSec, value] pairs; timeSec is seconds from the scene start.'. augmentToolSchemas sets description to Z_HINT on any object property named 'z' that has no description, and to KEYS_HINT on any property named 'keys' that has no description; existing descriptions are kept.
Create server/llm/glimmer/schema.test.ts with two inline ToolDefs built with zod.
acceptance: A tool with params z.object({ layerId: z.string(), z: z.number().optional() }) yields function.parameters.properties.z.description equal to Z_HINT
A property 'keys' typed as an array of [number, number] tuples gets KEYS_HINT, and a property that already has .describe('mine') keeps 'mine'
The output has type 'function', copies name and description, has no '$schema' key anywhere at the top level of parameters, and keeps the input order
A tool with no params properties still yields parameters of type 'object'

stories.title: Map chat messages to Ollama messages
stories.description: As a backend developer, I want conversation messages translated to Ollama's format so that tool results are matched by tool_name and the local-model rules are added for edits.
steps: Read server/llm/backend.ts (S2) to learn the exact ChatMessage and ToolCall shapes, in particular how an assistant turn records its tool calls and how a tool result records which call it answers; adapt the mapping to the real shapes and record any difference in notes. Read docs/hackathon/steps/step-09-open-weight-lane/design.md sections 4.1 and 6.

Create server/llm/glimmer/messages.ts exporting LOCAL_EDIT_ADDENDUM (the exact text: "(Local model rules) Make every change the user asks for in ONE turn by calling all the tools you need together. Do not explain. Do not call tools you do not need.\nTimes are seconds from the start of the scene. Scale is a fraction (1 = 100%). z is depth: larger = further from the camera, so the background has the largest z.") and toOllamaMessages(messages: ChatMessage[], opts?: { task?: 'storyboard' | 'build' | 'edit' | 'review'; parallelHint?: boolean }): OllamaMessage[].

Mapping: system, user and plain assistant messages pass through; an assistant message with tool calls becomes { role: 'assistant', content, tool_calls: [{ function: { name, arguments: <object> } }] }; a tool result becomes { role: 'tool', tool_name, content } where tool_name is found by matching the result's call id to the earlier assistant message's calls (fall back to positional order when ids are missing).

When opts.task is 'edit', append '\n' plus LOCAL_EDIT_ADDENDUM to the first system message (insert one if none exists). When opts.parallelHint is true also add the sentence 'You may call several tools in one turn.' once. For other tasks leave the system message unchanged.
Create server/llm/glimmer/messages.test.ts.
acceptance: A conversation [system, user, assistant with calls glimmer-0-0 (addScene) and glimmer-0-1 (addLayer), tool result for glimmer-0-0, tool result for glimmer-0-1] maps to 5 messages whose two tool messages have tool_name 'addScene' and 'addLayer' in that order
With task 'edit' the system content ends with LOCAL_EDIT_ADDENDUM exactly; with task 'storyboard' the system content is unchanged
With parallelHint true the sentence 'You may call several tools in one turn.' appears exactly once in the system content
Assistant tool_calls arguments in the output are objects, never strings

stories.title: Glimmer backend: native /api/chat with typed errors
stories.description: As a router maintainer, I want a Glimmer LlmBackend over Ollama's native chat API so that local edits use thinking off and the documented tool-call format.
steps: Read server/llm/backend.ts and server/llm/spark-backend.ts (S2) for the LlmBackend interface and how Spark builds its result, server/llm/glimmer/{parse,schema,messages,errors}.ts, and docs/hackathon/steps/step-09-open-weight-lane/design.md sections 3.2, 5.1 and 7.

Create server/llm/glimmer-backend.ts (an S2 stub today; fill it) exporting makeGlimmerBackend(opts: { baseUrl: string; model: string; task?: 'storyboard' | 'build' | 'edit' | 'review'; fetchImpl?: typeof fetch; timeoutMs?: number; keepAlive?: string; numCtx?: number }): LlmBackend, with id 'glimmer'. Defaults: timeoutMs 300000, keepAlive '30m'.

chatWithTools(messages, tools, o) POSTs JSON to `${baseUrl}/api/chat` with { model, stream: false, think: false, keep_alive, messages: toOllamaMessages(messages, { task, parallelHint: o?.parallelHint }), tools: toOllamaTools(tools) } plus options: { num_ctx } only when numCtx is set. Never send response_format. The turn number passed to parseOllamaChat is the count of assistant messages already in the conversation.

Error mapping: a fetch rejection that is not a timeout throws GlimmerError('unreachable'); AbortSignal.timeout expiry throws 'timeout'; a 404 or a body whose error text contains 'not found' throws 'model-missing'; a 500 whose error text contains 'parse' and 'call' throws 'tool-parse'; any other non-2xx throws 'http' with the status.
Create server/llm/glimmer-backend.test.ts with a node:http mock server on an ephemeral port that replays toOllamaResponse(loadTranscript('scene')) turns in order and records each request body.
acceptance: Driving the 4-turn scene transcript returns tool-call counts [1, 3, 2, 0], the last result has content 'DONE', and result.ms equals the transcript's ms for each turn
Every recorded request body has model 'muse-glimmer:30b-mlx', think false, stream false, keep_alive '30m', tools[0].type 'function', and no 'response_format' key
The backend's id is 'glimmer'; with numCtx 8192 the body has options.num_ctx 8192 and without numCtx it has no options key

A 404 reply with body {"error":"model 'x' not found"} throws GlimmerError code 'model-missing'; a closed port throws code 'unreachable'; a 500 reply with the text 'parse Glimmer call to addLayer: missing ATEM function_calls wrapper' throws code 'tool-parse'

stories.title: Closing-turn skip, request serialisation and context guard
stories.description: As an editor in Local mode, I want the backend to skip the redundant DONE turn, serialise requests and warn about truncated prompts so that local edits are as quick and safe as the hardware allows.
steps: Read server/llm/glimmer-backend.ts and docs/hackathon/steps/step-09-open-weight-lane/design.md sections 5.3, 5.6 and 5.7.

Edit server/llm/glimmer-backend.ts: add options skipClosingTurn?: boolean (the router sets it for task 'edit') and onWarning?: (message: string) => void. When skipClosingTurn is true and the conversation ends with one or more tool-result messages, every result content parses as JSON with ok true, and the preceding assistant message had at least one tool call, return { toolCalls: [], content: 'DONE', ms: 0, skipped: true } without any HTTP request. If any result has ok false (or is not valid JSON), send the request normally.
Serialise calls: chain chatWithTools through a per-backend promise queue so two concurrent calls never overlap; a rejected call must not block the queue.

Context guard: after each response compare usage.promptTokens with an estimate of the sent prompt (JSON.stringify of messages and tools, characters divided by 4). When promptTokens is below 60% of the estimate call onWarning('context truncation suspected (prompt_eval_count=<n> estimate=<m>)') and console.warn the same text.
Extend server/llm/glimmer-backend.test.ts using the edit-1 transcript and a mock server that counts requests and can delay replies.
acceptance: With skipClosingTurn true, the edit-1 flow (turn 1 returns 2 tool calls, all results {"ok":true}) makes exactly 1 HTTP request and the second chatWithTools returns content 'DONE' with skipped true
If one result is {"ok":false,"error":"x"} the second chatWithTools does send a request (2 requests in total); with skipClosingTurn false it also sends the request

Two simultaneous chatWithTools calls against a mock server that delays 50 ms are processed one after the other (the second request arrives after the first reply was sent), and a failing first call does not block the second
A reply with prompt_eval_count 10 for a prompt of about 4000 characters triggers onWarning with text containing 'context truncation suspected'; prompt_eval_count 1000 does not

stories.title: JSON mode with format, and local image review
stories.description: As a backend developer, I want JSON answers through Ollama's format field and an image reviewer so that structured outputs and frame review also work locally.
steps: Read server/llm/glimmer-backend.ts, docs/hackathon/steps/step-09-open-weight-lane/design.md sections 3.4 and 5.1 (use format, never response_format; images are base64 strings in the message's images field), and 06-contracts.md section 4 (MetaClients.spark.reviewImages signature).

Edit server/llm/glimmer-backend.ts: add chatJson<T = unknown>(messages: ChatMessage[], schema: object, validate?: (v: unknown) => T): Promise<T> to the returned backend object. It sends { model, stream: false, think: false, keep_alive, messages (toOllamaMessages), format: schema } and returns JSON.parse of message.content, passed through validate when given; non-JSON content throws GlimmerError('invalid-json').

Create server/llm/glimmer/review.ts exporting glimmerReviewImages(images: Buffer[], prompt: string, schema?: object, opts: { baseUrl: string; model: string; fetchImpl?: typeof fetch }): Promise<unknown>. It builds one user message { role: 'user', content: prompt, images: images.map(b => b.toString('base64')) }, sends think false and format = schema ?? 'json', and returns the parsed JSON (same error mapping as the backend).
Create server/llm/glimmer/review.test.ts and extend the backend tests using the mock server.
acceptance: chatJson sends a body whose format deep-equals the schema argument, with think false and stream false and no 'response_format' key, and returns the parsed object
Content '12s{' makes chatJson throw GlimmerError with code 'invalid-json'
glimmerReviewImages with two Buffers sends one user message whose images array has 2 base64 strings equal to buffer.toString('base64')
glimmerReviewImages with no schema sends format 'json'

stories.title: Local-mode state and Glimmer status with a 60 s cache
stories.description: As a developer of the router and the UI, I want one place for the Local-mode flag and Ollama's status so that decisions are consistent and cheap.
steps: Read docs/hackathon/steps/step-09-open-weight-lane/design.md sections 3.3, 4.3 and 5.4, and server/env.ts (S2) for the validated GLIMMER_BASE_URL, GLIMMER_MODEL and LOCAL_MODE keys (never read process.env for them).

Create server/llm/local-mode.ts exporting getLocalMode(): boolean, setLocalMode(v: boolean): void (module state; the initial value is the validated LOCAL_MODE from server/env.ts, 06 D-8, read lazily on first use; resetLocalModeForTests(initial = false) resets it), resetLocalModeForTests(), and getGlimmerStatus(opts?: { baseUrl?: string; model?: string; fetchImpl?: typeof fetch; now?: () => number; forceRefresh?: boolean }): Promise<LocalModeStatus['glimmer']> with the shape in design 4.3.

getGlimmerStatus: GET `${baseUrl}/api/tags` with a 1.5 s timeout; reachable = the request succeeded with a JSON body; modelPresent = some models[].name equals the model; when reachable also GET `${baseUrl}/api/ps` and set loaded = some models[].name equals the model (null when /api/ps fails). On failure return { reachable: false, modelPresent: false, loaded: null, error: <message>, ... }. host = the URL's host (for example 'localhost:11434'); checkedAt is an ISO string from now(). Cache the result for 60 seconds per (baseUrl, model); forceRefresh bypasses it.
Create server/llm/local-mode.test.ts with an injected fetch and clock.
acceptance: With /api/tags returning { models: [{ name: 'muse-glimmer:30b-mlx' }] } the status is reachable true and modelPresent true; with another model name modelPresent is false
When /api/ps lists the model loaded is true, when it lists nothing loaded is false, and when /api/ps fails loaded is null
Two calls 30 s apart cause 2 fetches in total (tags and ps once); a call 61 s later fetches again; forceRefresh fetches again immediately

A rejected fetch returns reachable false with a non-empty error string; getLocalMode is false when the injected env has LOCAL_MODE false, true when it has LOCAL_MODE true, and true after setLocalMode(true)

stories.title: Router: Local mode, API-failure fallback and tool denylist
stories.description: As an edit-loop maintainer, I want pickBackend to choose Glimmer or Spark by the documented table so that Local mode and fallback work without the loop knowing about them.
steps: Read server/llm/router.ts (the S2 stub: Spark-only bodies), server/llm/spark-backend.ts, server/meta/http.ts (the MetaApiError class and its status field), docs/hackathon/06-contracts.md section 6 D-5 and D-10, and docs/hackathon/steps/step-09-open-weight-lane/design.md sections 3.1, 5.2 and 5.5. Adapt names to the real code and record differences in notes.

Edit server/llm/router.ts: implement createRouter(deps: { makeSpark: () => LlmBackend; makeGlimmer: (task) => LlmBackend; getStatus: () => Promise<{ reachable: boolean }>; getLocal: () => boolean }) and export pickBackend(task, opts?: { local?: boolean; onFallback?: (info: { from: string; to: string; reason: string }) => void }): LlmBackend (the D-5 signature) built from the real defaults (makeGlimmerBackend with GLIMMER_BASE_URL, GLIMMER_MODEL, skipClosingTurn true for task 'edit').

Decision table: edit and review use Glimmer when opts.local === true or (opts.local === undefined and getLocal()) (an explicit opts.local, which S6's runEdit forwards from the chat request body per D-10, beats the global Local-mode default); storyboard and build use Glimmer only when opts.local === true; opts.local === false always means Spark without fallback. Otherwise Spark wrapped by withFallback.

shouldFallback(err): true for a MetaApiError with status 402 or >= 500, and for network failures (TypeError 'fetch failed', AbortError, TimeoutError); false for other 4xx and for anything else. withFallback tries Spark, and on shouldFallback and a reachable Glimmer calls opts.onFallback({ from: 'spark', to: 'glimmer', reason: <for example 'Meta API 402'> }) (console.warn when absent) and answers with Glimmer; when Glimmer is unreachable it rethrows Spark's original error.

Local edit tool denylist: when Glimmer serves task 'edit', wrap chatWithTools so tools named generatePlate, placeProduct, addSubject, replacePlate, proposeGenerate or reviewScene are removed before the call.
Create server/llm/router.test.ts with fake backends (makeFakeBackend from server/llm/fake-backend.ts or plain objects) covering the whole table.
acceptance: Local flag off: edit -> spark; flag on: edit -> glimmer and review -> glimmer; flag on with opts.local false: edit -> spark; flag on: storyboard -> spark; opts.local true: storyboard -> glimmer

Spark throwing a MetaApiError with status 402 and Glimmer reachable returns Glimmer's result and calls onFallback once with from 'spark', to 'glimmer' and a reason containing '402'; status 503 behaves the same; status 400 is rethrown and Glimmer is not called
Spark throwing TypeError('fetch failed') falls back to Glimmer when reachable; with Glimmer unreachable the original Spark error is rethrown
In Local mode for task 'edit' a tool list [generatePlate, setKeyframes, replacePlate] reaches Glimmer as [setKeyframes] only, while Spark receives all three
opts.local false never falls back: Spark's 503 is rethrown even when Glimmer is reachable

stories.title: pickReviewer: local or API frame review

steps: Read server/llm/router.ts (D-5: pickReviewer(opts?: { local?: boolean }) is part of the contract and S5b must call it), server/llm/glimmer/review.ts, docs/hackathon/steps/step-09-open-weight-lane/design.md section 3.4, and how S2's stub obtains the Spark reviewer (MetaClients.spark.reviewImages in 06-contracts.md section 4).

Make the Spark reviewer and the Glimmer reviewer injectable through createRouter so tests need no network.

Rules mirror edit routing: Glimmer when opts.local === true or (opts.local === undefined and getLocalMode()); opts.local === false forces Spark without fallback; otherwise Spark with the same shouldFallback and reachability fallback to glimmerReviewImages.
Extend server/llm/router.test.ts.
acceptance: With the local flag on, pickReviewer returns id 'glimmer' and calling reviewImages hits the injected Glimmer reviewer, never the Spark reviewer
With the flag off it returns id 'spark' and delegates to the injected Spark reviewer with the same arguments
Spark's reviewer rejecting with a 402 MetaApiError falls back to the Glimmer reviewer when reachable and calls onFallback once; a 400 is rethrown
With opts.local false a 503 from Spark is rethrown and the Glimmer reviewer is not used

stories.title: GET/PUT /api/local-mode handler
stories.description: As a UI developer, I want the Local-mode endpoints so that the toggle can read and switch Local mode from the browser.
steps: Read server/http/handlers/local.ts (the S2 501 stub registerLocalRoutes(app, deps) that S9 fills), server/http/routes.ts (how it calls it; never edit routes.ts), server/http/middleware.ts and auth.ts (S2: the passcode middleware guards mutating routes), docs/hackathon/06-contracts.md section 5 and D-1, D-6, and docs/hackathon/steps/step-09-open-weight-lane/design.md sections 5.4 and 7.
